returned_verdict.limits: Static read of the pasted module, tests and one report only; mitt_pilot.load_answers, mitt_temporal.unusable_reason and PatchTracker are not shown, so two things rest on the stated tracker/loader contract rather than inspection: that the answers/b*.json glob equals the file set load_answers actually opened, and that lost is terminal and a seed row only ends 'tracking' or 'lost'. Answer hashes are taken after load_answers consumed the files (no hash-at-consumption as frames have); tf32 and post_loss_matching are literals, not observed; platform.processor() yields a CPUID family string on Windows and is often empty on Linux. Test results and report numbers are the user's execution evidence; I checked only their internal arithmetic. Hashes and AI disagreement are not accuracy or provenance authentication; timestamps remain manifest-derived assumptions.
